utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: From Lolici told Mr. Rizvanovic about loud artillery fire coming from the direction of Sikirici -- Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Siljkovici. He said that he was somewhere in the area, I don't know precisely where, and that he was told by those people that the shelling was from Siljkovici, Jezestica, and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, prior to Mr. Rizvanovic's participation in this attack, you don't know if he had spoken with anyone in Srebrenica, do you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you don't know if he had spoken with anyone in Konjevic Polje about Siljkovici or Sikiric?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you don't know whether he'd spoken with anyone from Suceska or Pale?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, you also stated that he went in -- he went in the direction of Sukurici [phoen], or I should restate, Sikiric --

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And the reason that he had done that was because there was artillery located there. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was his reason. I said that he moved towards us to help us. From the direction of Siljkovici, where the artillery was, via Djermani. He came to our aid.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And had he contacted you or Ejub Golic during -- prior -- prior to him going to Siljkovici, did he contact either you or Ejub Golic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And the 400 men that he was with, you indicated some of them were from your area, there were pictures shown yesterday and you indicated that there were some people that you knew.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether at that moment he had 400 men. I know that 200 came to Cizmici. I don't know where the rest was, but he brought 400 to the area of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: He brought 400 to the area of Konjevic Polje or Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the area of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. And you don't know where the other 200 went?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you don't know whether they were engaged in attacks in other areas in that region?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you stated that Ejub Golic went towards -- and yourself included, went towards Veresinje?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, prior to doing -- to doing that, did you speak with Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And what time did you go towards this area?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall precisely at what time. So the shelling was heavy on the areas I mentioned yesterday but I don't know what time of day it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you said that there were about 100 to 150 men and only a third of them were armed?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And when Nurif Rizvanovic went towards Sikirici, you don't know Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what time he went there, do you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: But it was on the same day?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you stated that you left the area of Veresinje because your friend had stepped on a mine and you had to take him back. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were in the area of Veresinje moving towards Hrastik. I don't know how far it was exactly but we could see it and we came across a minefield and then I returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. And what time was that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I didn't have a watch.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, how far into the battle was your friend injured?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attack began in the morning, and I never wear a watch so I really don't know what time of day it was. I don't have a watch even today. I never used to wear a watch.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, how long had you been fighting, engaged in combat, before your friend stepped on the mine? Was it an hour, two hours later?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately two, two and a half hours. I believe that's how long the fighting lasted, in my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's how long you stayed or how long the fighting started? That's how long you stayed? That's what I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time between the moment we started moving forward and then the fighting itself and up to the moment when people stepped on the mines. That's the entire period.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So you stayed for the entire battle?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. That's what I'm seeking. So at some point you left before the attack was over, would that be correct, to take your friend back because you were concerned about him?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And the fighting continued in that area?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you have radio communication in your group? Did you have Motorolas or what is referred to as the RUP if you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: But at some point you later did come in possession of this -- of radio communication following this attack?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had no electricity. If you have a certain battery in mind, we had no electricity. We couldn't charge them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, did you have them? Did you have radios?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So leaving aside electricity, you had no radios?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You didn't have any radios up until, let's say, for all of 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never had any.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to refer you back to your testimony. I'm reading from page 39 yesterday's transcript. And keep in mind I'm not talking about August 8th at this point. I'm talking about later on in the year. "Question: There was a" -- I won't read out the whole question but I'll go to line 21. "Witness, were you attacked on the 31st of December 1992, as stated in a report? And you were shown a particular document." Do you recall being attacked on the 31st of December?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And in response, you said, "Yes, they attacked us on the 31st of December and there were thousands of shells that landed in the area where we were and they kept repeating by radio communication, 'this is your new year's present.' . The question was, "Can you remember the direction of the attack?" Answer: "The directions came from Hranca, Kravica, Jezestica, that is from all directions."

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's not agreeing. I notice that the accused -- sorry, that the witness was not agreeing with what you were stating. So I would suggest that we first give him the opportunity to state where he would like to register disagreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Please go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think I know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said that they informed us via radio communications. They were shouting that over the lines. They were throwing the shells across and because they were close they were shouting, well, "This is for you for the new year." But there were no radio communications involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So there was not correct when you said this yesterday and it was recorded as radio communications, that's not correct? I'm quoting your own words. Are you saying you didn't say that or are you saying that this is not correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we read specifically from yesterday's, or whenever it was, transcript? Because I obviously do not -- but can you read again what you have in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And from which line to which line so that the Defence can actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'm reading from page 39, beginning at line 21, there was a question, this is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is yesterday's?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: There is yesterday's transcript. It's -- the question was, "Witness, were you attacked on the 31st of December 1992, as stated in the report? "Answer: Yes. They attacked us on the 31st of December and there were thousands of shells that landed in the area where we were and they kept repeating by radio communications, this is your New Year's present." And that's in the transcript from yesterday, recorded as what was stated by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, now, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, unfortunately when I'm examining in chief I'm not able to follow the transcript. However, the witness did not say anything like that and we will ask for the audio tape in order to check that. He said that they were shouting over the lines. He didn't mention radio communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed. In the meantime, please, the technicians prepare the audio from yesterday, and we will revisit this topic or this particular point when we have that available. All right? In the meantime please let's go ahead. It's an important matter, obviously, and I prefer to have available -- how long would the technicians require? Do you have -- all right. Okay. Because we can actually go into the transcript and give him exactly the time when these words were supposedly or allegedly said, and we can go straight to that part of the transcript -- of the video recording. Yes, Ms. Richardson, please proceed with something else unless this really disrupts your -- I wouldn't like to disrupt your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, this is fine. I think I can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would like to have the witness be shown P84. The Territorial Defence municipal staff Srebrenica. Titled, "memo pad." And it is in Sanctions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right, the B/C/S or the English translations, ERN is 0211-5040-02115173. And the B/C/S -- excuse me, I'm sorry, I stand corrected. That's the B/C/S, I'm told. Just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I just stand corrected on the ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I ask for the assistance of either Prosecution or Defence? You have located where that extract is from. What the technicians require is the exact time, so please go into yesterday's -- I could do it myself but I either do this or follow what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's 11.05.10, I think, according to what I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour it starts at 11.07.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sometimes they are not in sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. And yesterday I think you had a problem in the beginning, or was it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, it depends on when one logs on to the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, from 11.00 to 11.15. That would cover it for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, from 11.00 to 11.15. Thank you. And thanks for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, I would like the witness to be directed to ERN number 02115093 and the English, it's 03090742 [sic]. Just to take you to the beginning of the minutes, this is from December 10th 1992 of the minutes of the Srebrenica OS staff meeting held on the 10th of December 1992. And it is page 38. And it is in Sanction. I see. All right. I'm just being instructed to give corrected ERN numbers. The ERN number would be 5 -- excuse me, 02115092. So -- and I'm reading towards the end of that particular page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you would look at the -- towards the end of that page, it says KM Pale, Glogova, RUP/from Cizmici goes to Glogova, stationary station on Pirica Brdo [phoen]. Now, if you would look at the next page -- before you answer my question, sir --

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear the beginning. There was some kind of interference. I really couldn't hear the beginning of what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unfortunately -- yes, I can actually read it. She asked -- Madam Richardson asked you as follows, sir, and she said "Now, sir, if you would look at the -- towards the end of the page, it says, KM Pale, Glogova, RUP from Cizmici, goes to Glogova, stationary station on Pirica Brdo." "Now, if you would look at the next page, before you answer my question" -- and that's where she was stopped. So please now refer him to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And it starts with ambush from Bratunac. Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to mention that in the Bosnian version, it does not say "in Glogova," it just says "in GL." And it does not say that the RUP is from Cizmici. GL in that area could mean all kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would appreciate if counsel not make submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But, but, but, wait, wait, wait. Let's -- let me see the original on the ELMO, please. Because if she is correct, you can ask the question what he thinks that GL means. If there is no RUP, you cannot suggest it to the witness. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the point is taken, if the translation is correct. What my objection was to the counsel stating for in the witness's presence that GL could mean anything, which could suggest to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Probably it will. I mean, in their language, one -- a single thing can be described in something like ten words. Sometimes 50 words.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, please. I can't even see Cizmici. I can see Pale. Yes, Glogova, K4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Cizmici, at the end of the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is here but I don't -- I don't -- I don't see RU -- unless the -- I don't see it. Where is the RUB?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The end of the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But there is Cizmici but not RUB.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: RUP, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: RUP. Yeah. I don't see it. And we have to be precise. I mean -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't even see the word RUP here but a very longer word which we cannot read as RUP without seeing the person who actually wrote it. I cannot read it as RUP. It says [B/C/S spoken] Then it says full stop, and then there is a word of five letters and then a much longer word and then it says something [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't help you because it's definitely not my area of specialisation Ms. Richardson, but if it's not important or that important let's move. And go straight to the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we can move.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If you -- if you look towards the next page, it says Glogova, Smajo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The third -- the third part of that -- the third paragraph of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And it lists just before the name Glogova, there is -- it says one station, Mandic, one RUP 12, Andrici, hand-held set. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have to go to the next page, yeah. That's he's seeing it, yes, do you see that or not? Yes, Ms. Vidovic? Put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours, Your Honours, please, they should look through these documents. It does not say "stanica" again, it simply says "one ST." That does not have to mean stanica, station. They should really read exactly what it says in the document. In the Bosnian it never says "stanica," "station" and that is why I asked for this document to be reviewed, the English version of the document to be reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me make a suggestion, in the interests of time, this is really -- I'll get back to this document on something else and I'll move on to the other question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour, just one comment which I think emerges from this, is that the problem is this interpretation is interpretive in the sense that whoever has produced the English version --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt but perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him finish, please. Please let him finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's simply there: We can see in many cases where there is a question mark and the person translating this has made a stab, had a guess on what the expansion should be, and that's -- to then put that to the witness he's not being -- basically, the original is not being put to him. It's someone's interpretation of what the words might stand for. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the problem is much more limited; however, I do agree that there is a problem. And it's endemic, I think, but the problem is least to the witness because at least he's got the original in front of him, which unfortunately I don't rely upon as we go along unless my attention is drawn -- when I say "my," it's our attention is drawn to the need to refer to the original. But the thing is this: If it's important let's go ahead with it. If it's not important, let's move, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: My only question is --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- Your Honour, we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What were you trying? If I may ask you. I know I don't have a right to ask you, but what were you trying to elicit from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my only question to the witness is whether or not he was aware that Cizmici or the area of Glogova had communication equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But then put the question straight and forward to him and then the rest can become a submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, that's my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I believe, sir, you've heard my question. Do you know if in December of 1992 the area of Cizmici or the wider Glogova area had communication equipment?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Is that no they did not have it, or, no, you don't know?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: That we didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, the other groups -- you talked about the recovery of weapons by the other groups, including your group. Do you know if the other groups were able to seize communication equipment during the different battles that they engaged in from May up until December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see it with anyone. I didn't see any radio stations in anyone's possession.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: But you didn't see it in their possession but there -- you can agree with me, can you not, that there is a possibility that they could have been in possession of it?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot agree because I was with Ejub Golic. I was the closest there to him so I would know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: But you also testify you were not with him all the time and you were not privy to all of the information that he had received. You previously testified to that, earlier today. So someone could have recovered -- my question is: Someone could have recovered a radio from one of these groups and have told him about it, and then you not be aware of it. Is that not a possibility?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't understand each other. I was in the area of Velika Glogova. Thus I was in the woods. Thus I was there with him. I wasn't like a belt all the time with him, sticking to him, but mostly I was there and I would know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And Cizmici is seven to eight kilometres away from the area you were in?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And there were armed groups there and they were engaging in battle and recovering weapons from the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an armed group, and not armed groups, in Cizmici, as far as I know, and I would probably have seen it when I came in August. I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. would have seen those radio stations but I never saw any.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, you said in August that you were in the area of Veresinje and that you took your friend back to Velika Glogova, Glogova, because he had been injured so you were not privy to everything going on in that attack that day, were you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say it like that. I returned my friend to the area of Cizmici and not to the area of Velika Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. But my point is: Once you left the area, you don't know what was going on in the area, do you? In Veresinje. Veresinje. Thank you. Because you weren't there.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out thus that fighting was still going on. So when people returned to Cizmici with Ejub Golic, they talked about what happened and I said yesterday that reinforcements had come from Kravica and that they had managed to push them back or return them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were you aware of whether or not Nurif Rizanovic, who came to the area with well-armed soldiers from the ABiH army, with weapons, do you know whether they had radios?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see. I didn't see that group that was in Cizmici, I didn't see that. I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So you don't know whether Rizanovic and the soldiers from Tuzla, well-armed soldiers, had radios, do you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also said that you were under the impression that Rizanovic was under the command of Tuzla. Now, during the time that Mr. Rizanovic was in your presence in Cizmici, how long would you say that meeting or conversation that you were part of lasted?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long. Approximately something like, well, I don't know, I didn't have a watch so I wasn't really following it but I think all of that was perhaps going on until 2.00 of that same day, the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And to be clear, Mr. Rizanovic and his armed men made their way down to Cizmici on the very same day that they engaged in the attack in Sikirici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the attack at -- I didn't understand which attack you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question. Where did Mr. Rizanovic and his men come from that day, when you met with them and there was this meeting?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like they were in the area of Lolici and they attacked one -- one of his groups attacked Siljkovici, the second group attacked Djermani and Stara Jezestica, and they came to Cizmici. Thus they did not take Siljkovici. There was a lot of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I understand that but my question is, so it was the same day that they ended up in Cizmici, having a conversation with Ejub Golic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I already said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And they didn't go to Velika Glogova where Mr. Ejub Golic usually stayed, did they?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, so -- I mean I told you that that day we were pushed out of Velika Glogova. I said that we were thrown out in the -- in early August from Glogova, and there was nobody in Glogova at the time of the Muslims, no Muslims were in Glogova at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Rizanovic came directly to Cizmici where Ejub Golic and other mean from his group had convened; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did any of the men in Ejub Golic's group participate with Mr. Rizanovic in the attack that he conducted in Sikirici? Siljkovici?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some men from Glogova were in Tuzla and they came with him. I cannot recall the names of those lads now, but there were such people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is: Not the men from Glogova who came with Mr. Rizanovic from Tuzla. I'm not talking about them. They were part of the 200 well-armed soldiers. I'm talking about the group, the four groups that you've talked about today, did any of those men in that group participate with Mr. Rizanovic in his attack?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So Mr. Rizanovic, on his own, conducting an attack in Sukerici -- Siljkovici, came down to Cizmici to where Ejub Golic and the other men had convened?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He came to Cizmici with that group of his.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And without having any communication with you, he came straight to Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any news about the video recording of yesterday? No. Would you require time for re-examination, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's say 20 minutes, about 20 minutes. Your Honours, and if I just may assist by saying that we agree, if that suits the Trial Chamber, what you did at one point for two judges to continue sitting so that we can continue, if this is a suitable solution for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will decide that later -- on that later on. Yes, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, you testified as well that Mr. Rizanovic and these men came, about 200 or 400, you heard about 400 but you actually saw 200, they were all well-armed, in uniform, and some of them wore berets? Would that be correct? Now the men in your area did not have uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were -- were you in contact with any of the fighters from Potocari or Pale or Suceska, in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And I take it you were not in contact with the Territorial Defence in Srebrenica either?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand whether the witness said yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness said "ne."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you had not seen Naser Oric prior to August of 1992? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I already said I saw him for the first time in January.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you don't know if the members of the Suceska TO, Potocari TO, or the Pale TO, or from Srebrenica itself possessed uniforms, do you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw uniforms, ever, on anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I'd like a videotape to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which videotape is it? I'm asking you for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 329.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: We are having problems with the sound at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Until this is fixed, let's move to another question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest is this. I'm actually discussing with Judge Eser, even if we agree that we proceed, two of us, alone, we'll still have to have a break, which, considering that we have gone beyond -- I mean it will be more than an hour and a half, we will be required to be of 30 minutes which would only leave us with about 10 minutes. So what I suggest is that you face reality. Either we decide here and now that this witness will stay here and will continue on Monday, which I wouldn't like to see happening, or else you reorganise your cross-examination and limit yourself to what you consider to be more important or more relevant, and the Defence will do the same and possibly cut down on the 20 minutes and everyone tries to sacrifice. Do you have any questions yourself? Because I may have but I'm prepared to renounce them so that we finish with there witness by 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, at this point I'm moving as quickly as I can and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not criticising you, please don't misunderstand me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I have taken out some portions already so everything that I do plan on referring to or asking the witness about is--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Let's not lose more time but the situation is as follows: That if you -- I'll ask you whether you're prepared to stop 20 minutes before 1.00. Then if you're not, that basically means that we are going to spill over on to Monday. There is no question about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'll take that into consideration as I'm moving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we still don't have the sound. So let me see if there is another area I can cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has it been fixed? No? No. It hasn't been fixed so let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall -- do you know anyone from -- who lives in Pale?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, following the -- following the attack on the 8th of August, you stated that individuals followed Zulfo Kumic [phoen] ... I'll repeat the question. There came a point that people left Cizmici and returned to Velika Glogova. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: The period following August of 1992. Because I believe you stated that Cizmici was overcrowded and that people returned to Velika Glogova.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After -- after -- after that, late summer, early fall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And they were -- they were led by a man called Zulfo Comic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And Ejub Golic stayed in Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take you to December of 1992, the 23rd and the 24th. Now, you stated that the area of Cizmici had been facing daily shelling. Would that be correct? From the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And that these Serbs were in the areas of Kravica, Jezestica, and they were heavily armed. Would you agree with that statement?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: They had -- you had encountered air strikes, they had infantry fighting, and very -- I think a lot more sophisticated weapons that your group had, such as automatic rifles and heavy guns?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had planes, tanks, everything. Praga's. We only had infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, and you said that they even had help from Serbia, correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And at this time, how many men -- no. I'll rephrase the question. You stated also that there were about 50 able-bodied men -- 500, excuse me -- and that you possessed about 100 to 150 weapons.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say precisely how many men there were, but I did say that there were between 100 and 150 pieces of guns, rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. And you said that these -- these men, able-bodied men, were registered?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. At this time I'm going to read from yesterday's transcript, page 33, line 22. When questioned, "When you say people -- when you say 'people,' what do you mean? Men, women?" "I mean able-bodied men, those registered as age-bodied men. There were about 500 such men, 400 to 500. I don't know the exact number." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So the transcript of your testimony from yesterday is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that in that way. I said I didn't mention the 500 men. And you can read out precisely what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I have just read it out, sir. Do you want me to read it out again?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No problem. "When you say people what do you mean? Men, women?" That's the question to you. Your answer was: "I mean men, able-bodied men, those registered as able-bodied men. There were about 500 such men, 4, 500, I don't know the exact number." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said they were registered or that somebody put them on a certain list. I just said that those were able-bodied men. Nobody ever registered them anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the substance of your objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I believe it's an erroneous transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I would suspect that it is indeed a case of an erroneous transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if that's what the witness has said, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And when you say able-bodied men, are you talking about men who are fit to fight and can engage in battle?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were men, all men, of that area. This is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I believe the video --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No it's not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the Glogova attack, you stated that Ejub Golic had a meeting and that it was decided that you would do something to stop the shelling and the attacks from Kravica and Jezestica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which meeting do you have in mind? And with whom? I said that he came in front of a group and that he said we either go to their assistance or we let them all be killed. This is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Indeed. And this was with respect to the attack of the 23rd, starting -- of the 23rd into the 24th. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 23rd, in the evening, or around midnight, we started moving towards Glogova from Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any other assistance, other than the 500 able-bodied men and the 100 to 150 weapons that they carried when you began this attack?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's convenient for you we will need to stop for about 15 to 20 seconds. Yesterday's video recording of the sitting is available. They will require just that amount of seconds roughly. Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object to the characterisation of the Prosecutor in her questions. She repeated several times, "attack on Glogova," whereas the witness kept saying yesterday that they were attacked by the Serbs and that they then launched a counter attack hence the question cannot be asked in that sense of an attack on Glogova on the 23rd. There was characterised differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please refer to it as a counterattack.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will. And just for the record, I made myself clear that they had been shelling on them and something and they decided to just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But please refer to it as a counterattack.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Counterattack, I will use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we stop for 15 to 20 seconds?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are going to stop now so that they put the ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's question, does the Chamber expect to us interpret?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think we need interpretation, yes. But when we reach that part, please tell us because I -- we need to know. Let's proceed. Are we stuck?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Witness, we were discussing the document of the 28th of December 1992. Concerning that I wanted to ask you this: After the 28th of December 1992, that is after the date of the report, did the situation change for you, who had Glogova in your hands? Did it grow worse or did it become better? "Answer: It grew worse. "Question: Do you remember particularly when it grew worse? "Answer: Yes, I do, on the 29th of December of 1992. "Question: All right. As of the 29th of December onwards, was the situation difficult or grave only on that day or did it -- was it becoming increasingly serious? "Answer: It increased, that is it became graver on the following days. "Question: Your Honours I would like to show another document to the witness. I would kindly ask the usher to distribute it. "This is a Bratunac Brigade command document dated 31st December 1992 and the number is 04363060. It is a combat report sent to the Drina Corps command by the Bratunac Brigade. "Witness, I will quote item 1 and item 2. It states, 'Up until 12.00, we did not encounter any significant enemy resistance. Stronger enemy forces are to be found on the road between Bratunac and Kravica in the place of Glogova. Our forces took over the elevation point Ladja 436 as well as elevation point KIK by the Lomanac river. For the time being, the activities continue as planned. In Bratunac there are 225 fighters in the action, 100 soldiers -- fighters participate of the infantry company. Antiaircraft platoon PAT 20-millimetre Praga, BOFORS, Bowing, and three tanks.' . "Witness, please, can you tell us whether those Serb forces attacked you on the 31st of December 1992 as was stated in the document? "Answer: Yes, they were attacking us on the 31st of December. Thousands of shells landed in the area where we were, and they were shouting across the lines, "This is your new years present." "Question: Can you remember where the attacks came from?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can stop there. This is basically what Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. we needed to hear. All right? So there is now what seems to be a confirmation that there was a -- transcript was -- did not reflect actually what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour, for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's very useful for you and for us and for the Defence of course. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank the technicians for having done this very quickly and so efficiently and the interpreters for having gone through it again. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were still trying to work out miracles and have this video --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I can move. I can move. It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, just keeping with the events of the 24th, just to recap, you stated that the Serbs were heavily armed and we talked about the artillery that they had and assistance from Kravica, Jezestica and Serbia et cetera. We talked about the fact that there were 500 men or so, approximate, in your group led by Ejub Golic and there were about 100 and -- to 150 weapons. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that concerning weapons, but I didn't mention the precise number of men. I didn't know that then and I don't know it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So are you saying that there were not approximately 400 to 500 men?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the number was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So you're retracting what you said yesterday in response to there being 4 to 500 men and you're now saying you don't know how many there were?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not retracting anything. I didn't mention the number. The group was large but I didn't mention figures.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Just so that don't misunderstand me, I'm talking about approximate numbers, not exact numbers, approximate. So were there approximately 400 to 500 men, as you stated yesterday?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You keep insisting and wanting me to say something. I can say that in my estimate, there were 4 to 500, but that's not what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can move, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So, sir, are you -- just to sum up the Glogova matter, you managed to successfully liberate Glogova or to take it from -- out of the hands of the Serbs on the 24th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the group of people headed by Comic Zulfo as well as civilians were in Glogova, and they had already been encircled, meant for this to be destroyed. We started moving on the 23rd of December of 1992. We fought in the morning, next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you were told what areas to cover of Glogova, I mean, you didn't all go in the same direction, did you, all 400 to 500 of you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were supposed to come in to deblock the road, going through Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So you had a specific task? I mean the groups.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is no task. We went to free those people and to drive the Serbs away.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you succeeded in doing that with about a hundred to 150 rifles and an unknown number of men, against the Serbs' weaponry, tanks, air supports, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just so that we understand each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Before you go into your explanation. I'd like you to answer my question. I have recapped what you've told us about the number of men and the number of rifles you had, and with respect to what you were facing from the Serbs. So my question to you is, if you want me to repeat it: With 100 to 150 rifles and approximately 4 lunch to 500 men, you were successful against the Serbs who were heavily armed with weaponry and antiaircraft and shelling from Serbia? You were successful, were you not? That is my question.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are five questions there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: My question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Richardson wants you to explain how come that you with your limited resources managed to beat the Serbs who were much better equipped than you were. This is basically what is being sought. Yes, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, well, Your Honour, I'm not surprised if the witness has difficulty answering that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not surprised either. I want to know what he was going to volunteer first.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, just to take just one element of the question, shelling from Serbia, you were successful, well, is he supposed to -- is his answer -- if he says, Yes, we were successful, does that suggest that he disabled heavy artillery in Serbia? I mean, of course, Ms. Richardson is deliberately --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If I can finish my objection, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Richardson is deliberately trying to characterise his answer as ridiculous, 150 weapons against all this weaponry. But it's not the suggestion that he went into Serbia and disabled all their heavy artillery. They succeeded in whatever they were doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And this is why I have tried to simplify the question by asking him to try and explain. If you have an explanation, how -- 400 to 500 Muslims, with about 150 rifles amongst them, managed to beat the Serbs, and regain possession of Glogova. This is what you're asked to explain, if you have an explanation because --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We started around midnight or 1.00 on the 23rd, from Glogova to Cizmici. Apart from the group that had already been in Glogova together with the civilians. So early in the morning, 5.00 or 6.00 in the morning, the fighting began. We managed to push them out of Glogova, and during the day then we were attacked by the aviation and artillery from Serbia. Perhaps that was the misunderstanding. So not in the morning when we were actually fighting them there, but later on during the day. Perhaps I wasn't very clear in my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very clear now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And by the end of the day on the 24th, you had - when I say you, the Muslim forces, fighters, groups - had successfully retaken Glogova. Would that be a correct assessment of the situation?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, I would like the witness to be shown Prosecution's Exhibit P84 again. And specifically it's ERN page for the English version 03090746; of the B/C/S it's 02115099. And I believe it's on page 42 of the English version. And we are trying to put it on Sanctions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's keep our fingers crossed that the translation is all right this time. Yes, Ms. Richardson? I don't see it on Sanction as yet, at least not on mine. I'll try again. Yes, it is on Sanction now. Yes, Ms. Richardson, your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Just for the record, this is from the minutes dated the 19th, 1992. And my question to you, sir, before I -- before I put this document to you and read from it, the Serb artillery that you were just talking about that existed on the 24th, did it continue to exist thereafter? I mean, the weaponry from Kravica, the Jezestica, the shelling, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. And the forces that you encountered in Glogova, were you engaged in hand-to-hand battle?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It is a village but we -- there was street-to-street fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And I take it there were a number of armed Serbs with their semi-automatic rifles and automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, I would refer you to the section, the portion, that begins with "Naser." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Right after that it says "Glogova". Now, it says, and I'm reading from the exhibit, "Naser, Glogova was the problem. They did not arrive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I see that the -- there may be a problem. Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't understand whether the Prosecutor mentioned the date to the witness concerning this document. I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think she did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did, yes, I did say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm speaking from memory. 19th, I think it was, or something, if I remember. I'm speaking from memory. 19th, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I did say that. But I can repeat it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not the 19th. Please repeat. It's the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam for that correction. It is indeed the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And, sir, if you read from the portion that I was just referring you to, read along with me of course following the B/C/S, it says "Naser, Glogova it was the problem. They did not arrive from the other side because there was an ambush at Bolom [phoen]. The operation must be repeated. The men from Glogova are asking to borrow 30 rifles." Now, before we go any further, you had a shortage of rifles, did you not, in your group?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Yes, yes. Of course, there was a shortage but I don't remember this. In English it says something up here. I don't understand what it says there. I don't understand what it says up in there in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You're supposed to be reading. Don't follow along on your screen. That's the English version for us English speakers. You're supposed to be reading from the B/C/S version of the document that's in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, could you please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Supposed to locate --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not understand this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's find -- you need to find ERN 02115099, according to what I have here. And it's a paragraph that -- I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Are you able to find that? It's on the B/C/S version, 02115099, and it's the very first sentence. It says, "Naser", then you see the word "Glogova."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can see it from here, I mean, but it's he who has to see it, not I. It's 3, 4, 8, 10, 11 lines from the top, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you see that, sir? Do you see the numbers 02 --

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. Great, thank you.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now I'll read it again: "Glogova was the problem. They did not arrive from the other side because there was an ambush in Bolom. The operation must be repeated. The men from Glogova are asking to borrow only 30 rifles." Now, my question to you is I believe you've already answered that there was a shortage of rifles in Glogova, among the armed groups.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a shortage of rifles throughout the whole period, as far as we are concerned. They didn't ask for any help. As far as I know there was no request for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what he said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So Ejub Golic could have asked for help; you don't know?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would. I mean, he was in Cizmici at the time so I would have known if he had asked for help. I would have known about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. But you were short on rifles?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were short of rifles throughout the whole war, throughout the entire 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving further down the page, it says, "Nezad

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: is requesting PVO/antiaircraft Defence of the town returns Soson's rifle. Each battalion will give two rifles to Glogova -- for Glogova" - excuse me - "Mirsad is asking when the rifles borrowed earlier will be returned. The attack on Glogova is planned for the 24th of December 1992." Now, sir, having read that, minutes from the OS staff in Srebrenica on the 22nd of December, I suggest to you that your group of 500 men, with 150 to -- with 100 to 150 rifles had assistance from Srebrenica and other forces, Muslim forces, and that is how you were able to capture Glogova. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can play the video now, and I can honestly say that I will not be done by 20 to, the time that you've given me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think there is no option. We are not going to curtail on -- given what has emerged now, I don't think that I can face Ms. Vidovic and say, cut down on your 20 minutes, if you're not prepared to stop 20 minutes before. So -- he will have to stay here and we will continue on Monday. Because also, I mean, I have questions and I wouldn't like to -- yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that I could cut it down to ten minutes, if you think that that would be of any help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if she finishes. I don't see Ms. Richardson finishing any time near, to be honest with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I'm not going to stop you. But on the other hand, if I am not going to stop you, I'm going to allow all the time that the Defence requires to re-examine the witness. Yes, let's see this video at last? Each time we have this video, we have problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "... talk about the attack Jezestica. This is Ejub Golic again. Rizvanovic. I explained about this. When they were supposed to go into Glogova the first time, what date was this? "The 8th of August 1992. Some action was also carried out on the other side at that time. They were -- they were supposed to go into the area of Glogova, that is Nurif Rizvanovic and the people that came with him, they were supposed to go around through Buljim and Susnjari and enter Glogova from there. However, what happened was that Nurif Rizvanovic fell into an ambush and then tried to break through under fire but as he didn't know the area very well, they didn't know the area, they had a lot of problems. As the others had already come out and were waiting and, in order to draw attention to themselves, they attacked. In the same way there was nothing organised here, there were no orders, this was -- this was done on their own initiative. "Were you involved in the planning process. "No. I don't know. Nobody planned this. Nobody planned this. This just happened unplanned. "You're telling me that Nurif came from Konjevic Polje to meet up -- to coordinate an attack from one side and then Golic was attacking from another side? There had to be some planning. "Then you didn't translate properly. I said that Nurif Rizvanovic was supposed to come from the area of Konjevic Polje. "Where? "Through Buljim."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. I just have a series of questions with respect to that last video.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, you've heard Naser Oric say with respect to Rizanovic and the area he was coming from, Konjevic Polje, and that they were supposed to go around Bolom but evidently there was a problem. Now, you also -- I just put to you Prosecution Exhibit P84 where that's being discussed by Naser Oric as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Firstly, that's -- well, Your Honour, I do object.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not done with my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, but if you're putting the exhibit, it didn't say Naser Oric, for a start. It says Naser and also whether it was Naser Oric or not in this interview is -- hasn't been said by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go back.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise the person on the video, sir, the person that's talking on the middle of the tape?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, it's -- that's not what's being contested, I think, by Mr. Jones. What's being contested by Mr. Jones is what appears on the face of the relative page from P84, where it says "Naser." They are not conceding that Naser means Naser Oric. I don't think he is contesting that the gentleman with the long hair and broad shoulders at the end of the screen is not Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's the first point and as far as the second, it was just to note that this witness hasn't actually said who the person is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I was responding to the second point first. If Mr. Jones's assertion is that the person -- that the witness hasn't said it's Naser Oric on the screen, is that -- is that -- is that what the point 2 was? In any event, Your Honour, we can move.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: With respect to what I read from you -- read to you from Prosecution's Exhibit 84, there was a Naser and he was talking about the problem at Glogova and there was an ambush at Bolom. Now, you've just heard that he's again speaking about Bolom, speaking about a Mr. Rizanovic, and that they were supposed to come from Konjevic Polje and go around Bolom but evidently there was a problem. Now, that information given by the person, Naser, in the memo pad and the person on the screen Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that we are looking at, is, would you say, similar information being given by both?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need the witness to tell you that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I would like him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have got eyes and we have got ears and we can establish whether it's similar or dissimilar or, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And draw conclusions if we need to because it may not be that relevant at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, were you aware, sir, that on the 8th of August, there were other actions being conducted, other than the one that you were involved in? Veresinje?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get the translation of this last part.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. If he hasn't had the interpretation of this last part, he needs to have it. Ms. Richardson asked you the following: "Now, were you aware, sir, that on the 8th of August, there were other actions being conducted, other than the one that you were involved in? Veresinje?" That's what I have in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's proceed. Did you say anything else that I missed?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that's pretty much it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And did you later learn, if you didn't know it on the 8th of August of 1992, that actions had been engaged in involving Muslim fighters in the areas of Zaluzje, in the areas of Beleca [phoen]. Excuse me, not Bileca, excuse me. So just to repeat so you're not confused, the areas of Zaluzje, Andrici, Kunjerac and, I believe, you've told us already that there was an action in Sikiric and Siljkovici. So my question is were you aware that these other places that I've just stated had been involved -- there were Muslim fighters involved in those areas as well, on the 8th of August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about these attacks and the villages that you mentioned, one of them I didn't really understand which one it was and these other villages mentioned, they are about 40 to 50 kilometres away from us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Well, the one that -- I'll read them out again, Zaluzje?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Zaluzje, Andrici, Kunjerac, Sikiric and Siljkovici, and the question was not whether you knew of any attack on the 8th of August of 1992 then, but whether you came to know about any attack that happened on that day later, whether you later came to know that there was an attack on some or more, or one or more of these villages on the 8th of August 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I didn't find out other than Siljkovici. Except for Siljkovici, I didn't -- anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were you to learn of those other operations, would you consider ... I'll rephrase the questions. Had those operations taken place, would it have been just a coincidence that the attack that you yourself was involved in also occurred on August 8th?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question simply is not clear to me. I said that these villages are about 40 to 50 kilometres away from us, and that I have nothing to do with that. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. My question is: Regardless of the distance of the villages, had you learned of those attacks, that they did in fact take place. To you, this would be a coincidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But again, I mean, put the question -- you're in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll put the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you aware of any plans to launch an all-scale attack on all these villages on the 8th of August of 1992? Did you ever become aware of that? Either then or later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. Now the question is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, at this time we will be playing another video. It's P517 and there are three clips.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Sir, if you would just look at your monitor that's in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recognise that individual who is in the centre of the photograph? Not the one with the coloured shirt but the one with the sunglasses on in the centre.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The picture is a little bit unfocussed. Maybe it can be a little sharper, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. Is that better?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the man wearing the sunglasses?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Is that something you recognise as Dr. Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those first few days, I didn't see myself personally but I heard that Nedret Mujkanovic had arrived. I didn't actually see him until I got to the hospital on the 7th of January, the hospital in Srebrenica. That was the first time that I saw this man. I didn't see him before. I never saw him in a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that it is Nedret or that it isn't Nedret.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. But however, the person on the screen is wearing a camouflage uniform, is he not?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the person in the camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. And just for the record this video is dated 19th of August 1992. We can play it a little bit more and the time is 3.17.2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, those individuals on the screen, do you recognise anyone there? I know the picture is not the best. Any of them seem familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just looking at it like that, the way I saw him later, that could be Naser in the camouflage uniform. I did used to see him later in uniform and this is the same build.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: When you say Naser, you mean Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And in this picture, he's wearing a camouflage uniform, is he not?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that -- the picture is not sharp enough to me. I cannot -- well, you would say that it was a camouflage uniform, yes. You would say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And there are other people in that scene with camouflage uniforms, are there not? We can go back a bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You see the person to the right of the screen, next to the person wearing the reddish colour shirt? Is that person wearing a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not sure myself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot see it. I can't see it properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. That's fine. We'll move to the other clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, sir, you stated before that you were not in contact with Srebrenica or any of the other territorial units in the surrounding area, and I take it you were not aware if they had uniforms or not.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know, and I didn't see people like that. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, you recall saying that in August, Rizanovic's men had uniforms and now, although you didn't know it at the time, having seen this video, do you now agree that there were other Muslim fighters in the area in August of 1992 with uniforms?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, I said when I saw the first uniforms, in the month of August, on the 8th of August, I saw the first camouflage uniforms that came.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's what you saw. But having now seen this video, that's dated the 19th of August 1992, can you agree that there were other Muslim fighters, including Naser Oric, who you've identified, wearing -- who owned and wore camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this was Naser Oric. I didn't see him before. Well, more or less, judging by this, I mean it could be him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And whether it's Naser Oric or not, do you agree that there are uniforms existing in the area, other than Rizanovic, in August of 1992? Having seen the video.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You don't agree. All right.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't see it, I cannot agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, at this time I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Richardson. Sir, I'm afraid you'll have to return on Monday. We haven't finished. Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one addition to the transcript. The witness said "no, no, I don't agree because I did not see it," and here we only have "I did not agree." His answer was that he did not agree because he did not see it himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think I heard that -- I heard that in the interpretation process, yes, definitely I heard it. All right. You will receive all the attention you require and your family will be informed that you need to remain here, unless arrangements are made to take you and bring you back again but I don't think that will be the case and we will continue on Monday in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to remind the witness not to speak with anyone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and please, sir, just -- I wish to remind you what I told you yesterday and before, that you are not to communicate with anyone or let anyone communicate with you on the matters related to your testimony, the subject matter of what you're giving evidence about. Of course, you can speak to your family, you can contact them and they can contact you, but that's about it. Not on the subject matter of your testimony. Did I make myself clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just one question. If somebody comes, if somebody comes from my area, perhaps -- I mean, am I allowed to just speak with them like that or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am not here to give you advice. I think the Victims and Witnesses Section will give you advice on that but if I were you, I would be very cautious. You would always be running a risk. We will spend maybe an hour or so trying to find out what you talked about, who was he or she, and why did you have to speak to him or her? And it goes on and on. So what I would suggest to you, particularly if you see other persons from your area in the same hotel where you are staying, or in the street where you may be walking, escorted, I would suggest that you might think that these may be witnesses too and that you would -- it would be wiser for you to avoid talking to them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can assure you that there will be eyes around you. So, yes, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I just make two very quick points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, can Judge Eser leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because it's past 1.00 already. Okay. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Also, if this is a submission that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the witness can leave as well. Where is the usher? Usher, can you please escort the witness out and make sure that the unit will now make all the necessary arrangements. I wish you a nice weekend, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact the first point --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that [microphone not activated] show up in the camera while you are talking. That's all. All right. Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. The first point is actually an apology from my side. I checked the transcript and, in fact, it had been suggested to the witness already that it was Naser Oric speaking in the interview during examination-in-chief. I apologise for that. I don't want to mislead anyone. The second point perhaps should in private session if we can go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private. One moment, I need to check. That's not on -- this is not working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
